cards.title: Exponential circuit lower bounds for 3-SAT
cards.formal:
For the explicitly encoded \(n\)-variable 3-SAT function \(\mathrm{SAT}_n\) below, do there exist constants \(c>0\) and integer \(n_0\ge1\) such that
\[\forall n\ge n_0,\qquad \operatorname{CC}(\mathrm{SAT}_n)\ge 2^{cn}?\]
The circuit lower bound is against arbitrary nonuniform Boolean circuits of fan-in at most two. Its exponential parameter is the number \(n\) of variables, not the number of input bits in the clause-incidence encoding. The card retains this previously recorded variable-parameter specialization of the source’s exponential-SAT conjecture.
cards.definitions:
Fix an integer \(n\ge1\) and variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). A clause is a disjunction of zero, one, two or three literals on distinct variables. Each literal is either \(x_i\) or \(\neg x_i\). The empty clause is false. Clauses never contain both signs of one variable or repeated variables. The list contains
\[M(n)=\sum_{j=0}^{3}2^{j}\binom{n}{j}\]
clauses, with \(\binom{n}{j}=0\) when \(j>n\). Order them first by their length, then lexicographically by their increasing tuple of variable indices, then lexicographically by their sign bits, with 0 meaning positive and 1 negated.

An input is a bit vector \(b\in\{0,1\}^{M(n)}\). Its \(i\)-th bit specifies whether clause \(i\) is included. Let \(\Phi_b\) be the conjunction of exactly those included clauses; the empty conjunction is true. Define
\[\mathrm{SAT}_n(b)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists a\in\{0,1\}^{n}\text{ satisfying }\Phi_b.\]
Every input vector is valid. Formulas are specified in full, not by a circuit or oracle that answers clause queries. All assignments are permitted; there is no uniqueness, sparsity or satisfiability promise. This representation includes clauses of width at most three. In ordinary lists, repeated literals can be removed, tautological clauses discarded and duplicate clauses merged without changing satisfiability.

A competing circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with \(M(n)\) input bits and one designated output. Each gate computes any Boolean function of at most two bits, the full \(B_2\) basis. Free constant sources 0 and 1 are allowed. Gates may have arbitrary fan-out and the depth is unrestricted. The gate count charges one per gate, including a unary gate, while input nodes, constants, wires and the output designation are free. The circuit must compute \(\mathrm{SAT}_n\) exactly on every \(b\). Its minimum possible number of gates is \(\operatorname{CC}(\mathrm{SAT}_n)\). A different circuit may be chosen independently for every \(n\), with no algorithm required to generate that family.

The circuit has \(M(n)=\Theta(n^3)\) inputs, so the conjectured size is \(2^{\Omega(n)}=2^{\Omega(M(n)^{1/3})}\). A claim exponential in the raw input length would be a different target and is not asserted. Switching between \(B_2\) and the bounded-fan-in AND/OR/NOT basis changes size by at most a fixed constant factor, preserving the existence of a positive exponential lower-bound exponent after adjusting constants.

The quantifiers are almost everywhere in the variable count: one positive exponent \(c\) must work at every sufficiently large \(n\). Their exact negation is
\[\forall c>0\ \forall N\ge1\ \exists n\ge N:\quad \operatorname{CC}(\mathrm{SAT}_n)<2^{cn}.\]
The integers \(n_0,N,n\) and real \(c\) have the domains just stated. A size bound \(2^{o(n)}\) at all lengths would imply the negative answer, but is stronger than this negation, which permits different favorable lengths for different exponents.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed eventual exponential circuit lower bound for the exact total function family defined here. A positive answer must establish one fixed \(c>0\) and threshold \(n_0\), and prove the lower bound against every correct circuit at every \(n\ge n_0\). A negative answer must establish the quantified negation stated above. Lower bounds only for formulas, monotone circuits, bounded depth, uniform algorithms or restricted proof systems do not meet the criterion. A uniform exponential-time upper bound with a fixed positive exponent remains compatible with a smaller positive lower-bound exponent. Neither a conditional theorem nor an oracle-relative theorem alone resolves this unconditional target. Asymptotic quantifiers are exact; numerical acceptance tolerance is not applied to exponents or big-O notation.
cards.why: An exponential unrestricted circuit lower bound for 3-SAT would establish a quantitative limit on even nonuniform solutions to a canonical NP-complete problem. Fixing the variable parameter makes its relationship to exponential-time hypotheses precise without assuming that algorithmic and circuit lower bounds are interchangeable.

importance.reason: A sweeping quantitative lower-bound target for the canonical efficiently verifiable problem, directly connected to nonuniform complexity and the foundations of exponential-time algorithms.

progress.text: Impagliazzo, Paturi and Zane establish sparsification and reductions preserving subexponential variable-parameter complexity.
Williams proves NEXP lower bounds for constant-depth ACC circuits.
Conjecture 5.7 poses exponential circuit hardness for SAT; the card retains an explicit variable-parameter version.
Li–Yang prove a \(3.1N-o(N)\) unrestricted two-input-basis bound for explicit affine dispersers.
The PPSZ analysis reports a smaller randomized exponential upper bound for general 3-SAT; the base remains strictly greater than one.

cards.status_note: Source-open with a bounded literature check through 16 September 2026. The original SAT circuit conjecture and the card’s previously documented variable-parameter specialization were checked. The sparsification theorem, Li–Yang main statement, Williams’s restricted ACC theorem and the 2026 PPSZ preprint’s unique/general statements were read; none gives a resolution of the defined total 3-SAT circuit target. No matching unconditional exponential lower bound or refutation was located. The PPSZ numerical certificate was not independently rerun, and the preprint is identified as such; no exhaustive present-status certification is claimed.

context_blocks.text: Checking a proposed assignment is efficient. The conjecture says that determining whether an assignment exists needs exponentially many gates in the variable count, even when each input length gets its own independently designed circuit. It is a quantitative lower-bound demand beyond merely excluding polynomial-size circuits.

The fixed input representation separates two quantities that are often both called size. There are \(n\) variables, but \(\Theta(n^3)\) possible distinct clauses and therefore that many incidence bits. Polynomially equivalent encodings need not preserve claims exponential in their raw bit length; fixing both quantities is essential.

Exhaustive assignment testing gives the unconditional upper bound \(O(M(n)2^n)\) on circuit size. Thus the conjecture concerns the presence of some positive exponential lower exponent, while allowing improvements in its constant.

The sparsification lemma writes a fixed-width CNF as a disjunction of at most \(2^{\varepsilon n}\) sparse formulas for each fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), with linear clause bounds depending on \(\varepsilon\) and the width. This supports reductions in exponential-time complexity. It does not convert a lower bound for uniform algorithms into one against arbitrary nonuniform circuits.

Li and Yang prove a \(3.1N-o(N)\) gate lower bound for suitable explicit \(N\)-input affine dispersers. It is a full-basis linear lower bound for particular functions, not an exponential bound for SAT. Counting yields much larger bounds for most truth tables but does not identify SAT among them.

Williams’s lower bound excludes polynomial-size ACC circuits for a language in nondeterministic exponential time. ACC imposes constant depth, unlike this card’s circuits, and the hard language is not asserted to be SAT. Both distinctions prevent that theorem from resolving this question.

Jiang and Cai’s July 2026 preprint reports an \(O^{*}(1.307031578^n)\) randomized running-time bound for general 3-SAT, with a slightly smaller base for unique 3-SAT; \(O^{*}\) suppresses polynomial factors. The reported improvement remains within exponential time. It is an upper-bound claim in a preprint, not an unconditional lower bound for exact circuits.

A positive answer would imply \(\mathrm{NP}\not\subseteq\mathrm P/\mathrm{poly}\) and hence \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\). A negative answer need not imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\): circuit sizes such as \(2^{\sqrt n}\) would already defeat every positive eventual exponential lower exponent while remaining superpolynomial, and nonuniform circuits need not yield an efficient uniform algorithm.

sentences: The question asks whether n-variable 3-SAT requires Boolean circuits of size at least two to a positive constant times n at every sufficiently large n.
Inputs are complete incidence vectors for all clauses of width at most three, giving Theta(n cubed) input bits.
The circuit model permits every two-input Boolean gate, arbitrary sharing and independent nonuniform designs at each length.
Known restricted-circuit lower bounds and randomized exponential-time improvements do not settle this unrestricted lower-bound target.
A complete answer must prove the eventual exponential bound or its exact quantified negation in Lean.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Inactive records are archived outside the catalogue, exports and editorial work. Their content, stable IDs and reasons are retained; imports cannot reactivate them. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Inactive cards, including resolved records, are archived outside the ranking without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.

benchmark_selection.basis: Individual editorial review of saved titles, importance rationales, problem statements, source notes and working summaries. This is a review of importance and topical diversity, not a fresh verification of open status or completion of draft formulations. Importance scores are preserved.
